blocks.x: After several years of being an outcast in Hollywood due to his personal troubles, Johnny Depp is all set to make a grand mainstream return with this year's Ebenezer — it's a new take on A Christmas Carol, directed by Ti West. There are also reports of Depp being courted to reprise his Oscar-nominated role as Jack Sparrow in a new installment of the Pirates of the Caribbean film franchise. At the peak of his popularity, Depp was considered the rare movie star capable of delivering box-office success and awards attention. He had a remarkable partnership with director Tim Burton that lasted more than two decades. Now, one of their most successful movies together is about to be removed from Netflix, leaving viewers with only a few days to check it out.

The movie in question was released theatrically in 2005, emerging as a massive hit. It grossed $475 million at the worldwide box office against a reported budget of $150 million, becoming Burton's top-grossing movie until it was overtaken by Alice in Wonderland in 2010. The 2005 film was based on a classic children's novel by Roald Dahl, which had previously been adapted into a popular movie starring Gene Wilder in the 1970s. Burton's version was darker, which many critics pointed out. The movie now holds a "Certified Fresh" 83% score on the aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, with the veteran critic Peter Travers describing it as a "treat for twisted children."
